summary: ST's 300 mm wafer fab in Agrate Brianza, Italy, which ST intends to become its flagship high-volume site for smart power and mixed-signal technologies. The fab was qualified for production in 2023 with slightly more than 1,000 wafers per week installed, starting with mixed-signal processes. Under its April 2025 footprint plan ST aims to double capacity to 4,000 wafers per week by 2027 and to add modules up to 14,000 wafers per week depending on demand; ST still described the fab as ramping up in November 2026.

milestones.note: Qualified for production in 2023 with slightly more than 1,000 wafers per week of installed capacity.

sources.title: Report on Form 6-K dated March 21, 2024 (STMicroelectronics 2023 Annual Report)
STMicroelectronics details company-wide program to reshape manufacturing footprint and resize global cost base
Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

notes: The 2023 annual report says smart power and embedded non-volatile memory processes were to be phased in after mixed-signal. ST's 2025 annual report lists the fab as Agrate Fab 3, running analog CMOS, BCD and embedded non-volatile memory processes, says it is currently shared with Tower Semiconductor, and plans 2026 spending on its ramp-up. The April 2025 plan targets 4,000 wafers per week by 2027 and modular growth to 14,000; these are weekly figures and are not converted into a capacity metric. The April 2025 plan is cited from ST's release distributed through GlobeNewswire; the previously cited I-Connect007 copy could not be read during the November 2026 technology update. Tower Semiconductor's own equipment line in part of the same cleanroom is recorded separately as tower-fab-10-agrate.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Codex): a second agent reopened every cited source and checked the record and technology additions against them.
review.changes: Added the three processes explicitly listed for Agrate Fab 3 in the 2025 annual report; replaced the inaccessible I-Connect007 copy with the same ST release via GlobeNewswire and retained separate scope for Tower’s line.
